key_insight: Continuous wearable temperature patterns can help machine learning distinguish engraftment fevers from other causes in hospitalized HCT patients.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support faster fever triage and more targeted early management when the cause of fever is unclear during hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
method: Monitored axillary temperature every 2 minutes with an FDA-cleared wearable sensor during hospitalization.
Extracted time-series features from 1 hour before to 3 hours after fever onset.
Trained and tested supervised machine-learning models using repeated stratified 5-fold patient-level cross-validation.
evidence_signal: In 68 clinically independent fever episodes from 90 HCT patients, logistic regression performed best, reaching 94% specificity for engraftment fevers with mean AUROC 0.88 ± 0.10.
watch_item: The model was evaluated on a relatively small, single clinical context dataset, so broader validation is needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: Rapid diagnosis of fever etiology using wearable temperature monitoring and machine learning
